subject: social
title: City, Town or Farm
about: Urban, suburban and rural places: tall buildings, buses and crowds in a city versus fields, barns and tractors on a farm, what you find in each and how people get around. NC 1.G.2.1 (how the land shapes where and how people live) and 1.G.2.2 (how people change the land with buildings, roads and farms).
tip: On a drive, ask him: is this a city, a town or the country, and how can he tell?

cards.q: Skyscrapers, taxis and crowds of people. Which kind of place is this?
cards.note: Cities are crowded, so buildings grow up tall instead of out wide.

cards.q: Open fields, a barn and a tractor. Which kind of place is this?
cards.note: Farms need lots of open land for crops and animals.

cards.q: A busy city area with crowds and tall buildings is called...
cards.note: Urban means city. Urban areas have the most people.

cards.q: Land out in the country with farms and only a few houses is called...
cards.note: Rural means country. Farms and forests are in rural areas.

cards.q: A neighborhood of houses and yards just outside a city is called a...
cards.note: Suburban means in a suburb. Many families live in a suburb and drive into the city.

cards.q: What do we call a very, very tall building in a city?
cards.note: A skyscraper is so tall it seems to scrape the sky.

cards.q: In a city, many families live in one tall building. What is each home in it called?
cards.note: An apartment building has many homes stacked on top of each other.

cards.q: On a farm, what building keeps animals, hay and tools safe and dry?
cards.note: A barn is a big farm building. Horses, cows and hay stay inside.

cards.q: Where would you most likely see cows and chickens?
cards.note: Farm animals need open land, barns and fields of grass.

cards.q: On a farm in the country, are your neighbors close by or far apart?
cards.note: Farms are big, so the next house can be far down the road.

cards.q: Where would you hear the most car horns and buses?
cards.note: Cities are busy and noisy, with cars, buses and taxis everywhere.

cards.q: How do many people get around in a big city?
cards.note: Cities have buses, subways and taxis, so not everyone needs a car.

cards.q: What big machine do farmers drive to work in their fields?
cards.note: A tractor pulls plows and wagons across the fields.

cards.q: How do most families in a suburb get to the store?
cards.note: Suburbs are spread out, so most families drive.

cards.q: In a crowded city, where do kids go to play on grass?
cards.note: People build parks in cities so everyone has green space to play.

cards.q: Which is bigger: a town or a city?
cards.note: A town is smaller than a city, with fewer people and shorter buildings.

cards.q: Fruits, vegetables and milk come from which kind of place?
cards.note: Food is grown on farms, then trucks carry it to stores in towns and cities.
